(Dated this the 06th day of November, 2025)
The petitioner is the accused in Crime No. 872 of 2024 of Kuthuparamba Police Station which is now pending as SC No. 154 of 2025 of Fast Track Special Court, Mattannur.

The offences alleged against petitioner under Sections 376(2)(i), 354, 354-B, 328,
342 and 366 of IPC.

2. The prosecution case is that on 26.09.2023, at about 9 am, the accused took the defacto complainant who was his class mate, in his car saying that he has to discuss something with her and on the way he caused her to drink some juice containing some intoxicating substance and thereafter he took her to a room in Royal Plaza at Mannar and committed rape upon her, took her nude photographs, threatened to destroy her life in case she discloses the incident to others and thereby he alleged to have committed the aforesaid offences.
3. According to the learned Counsel for the petitioner, it is a false case foisted against him due to some property dispute and therefore he prayed for quashing all further proceedings against the petitioner.
The learned Public Prosecutor as well as the learned Counsel for the 3 rd 2025:KER:85534 respondent strongly opposed the petition.

Relying upon the decision of this Court in K.S Sivarajan v. State of Kerala(Crl.MC.No. 5412 of 2020), the learned Counsel would argue that if the criminal proceedings are found to be manifestly frivulous or vexatious or instituted with the ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance, the same is to be looked into by the court while considering an application under Section 482 Cr.PC.
4.

sentences.text: On a perusal of the FI Statement and the records produced by the Prosecution, it can be seen that the petitioner who was a classmate of the defacto complainant pretending to have some discussions with her took her in his car and caused her to drink some juice containing drugs and thereafter took her to a room in a lodge and committed rape upon her.
The allegations leveled against the petitioner are very serious in nature constituting the offences alleged against the petitioner.

Even if there is any Sathyan Aniyeri vs State Of Kerala on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182517486/
2 property dispute between the petitioner and the respondent as contended by the learned Counsel for the petitioner, the same is not enough at this stage to disbelieve that the allegations raised against the petitioner, especially because the prosecution has established a strong prima facie case constituting the 2025:KER:85534 offences alleged against the petitioner.

sentences.text: Therefore, the prayer for quashing further proceedings against him cannot be allowed.
I do not find any merits in this Crl.MC and as such it is dismissed.
